name: v4.1.2-beta.1 — Updates Through the Engine and a Smooth Quit
body:
## What's Changed

This beta routes the app's own downloads through the engine, so updates download like any other download. Quitting from the tray no longer freezes the app, the close dialog can remember your choice, and the add window opens torrents at their final size.

### ✨ New Features

- **Close action** — the close dialog has a "Remember my choice" option, and General settings sets what the close button does: ask, minimize to the tray or quit (#778)

### 🛠 Improvements

- **Downloads through the engine** — update packages and metadata, remote `.torrent` files, tracker lists, the BT blocklist and ED2K bootstrap lists are downloaded by the engine with multiple connections and the configured proxy; update packages are verified with the updater signature before install. When the engine is not running, the app downloads them directly (#775)
- **Update dialog** — the status icon uses a tinted status color instead of a fixed green background

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed the app freezing when quitting from the tray or Dock; quitting now waits for the engine and services to stop without blocking the window system (#774)
- Fixed the add window growing abruptly when opened with a torrent file, and the form emptying while the window closes

name: v4.1.1 — Aria2 Next 3.0.9 and Windows Fixes
body:
## What's Changed

This release bundles Aria2 Next 3.0.9 for all platforms. Downloads finish without a slow tail, a retried download no longer corrupts its file, and a slow IPv6 route no longer holds a download back. It also fixes the Windows installer and caption buttons, external links, repeated clipboard prompts and RPM upgrades from a beta.

### 🛠 Improvements

- **Aria2 Next 3.0.9** — a slow connection hands its remaining range to idle ones at the end of a download (#762); connections move off an address family that is several times slower, so a broken IPv6 route no longer keeps a download at a crawl; connections that fall far behind are replaced
- **Clipboard** — a copied link is offered once per run, also after the main window is recreated from the tray or the link was already used in the add window (#751)
- **Browser takeover** — when the engine receives a verification page instead of the file, Rayburst takes over from the address the browser actually landed on (rayburst-connect#104)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed corrupted downloads after a retry: the unwritten part of a preallocated file is no longer counted as downloaded, and a server that rejects extra connections with 403 lowers the connection count instead of failing (#767)
- Fixed the Windows installer failing to stop running processes (#756)
- Fixed the caption buttons not reacting to hover or clicks on Windows 10 (#755)
- Fixed links in the update notes opening inside the app; links that leave the app open in the system browser (#764)
- Fixed a window hidden to the tray reappearing when the GNOME session locks (#759)
- Fixed a paused multi-file torrent asking for its file selection again (#754)
- Fixed RPM upgrades from a beta to the stable release being refused as a downgrade (#766)

name: v4.1.0 — Rebuilt Engine, Verified Handoffs and a Floating Window
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Rayburst 4.1 needs Rayburst Connect 2.1.2 or later.** Browser handoff was rebuilt for this release. With Connect 2.0.x the extension shows "Desktop version not supported" and the browser keeps its downloads. Update the extension from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/ofeajdebdjajhkmcmamagokecnbephhl), [Edge Add-ons](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/loojjolhejmakcdlbidigoniobfanjlb) or [Firefox Add-ons](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/rayburst-connect/). Connect 2.1.2 and later also work with Rayburst 4.0.

## What's Changed

Rayburst 4.1.0 is the largest update since 4.0 and brings eleven betas to the stable channel. It moves to the rebuilt Aria2 Next 3 engine, bundled here as 3.0.8, which replaces the event loop inherited from aria2 with Boost.Asio, libcurl, libtorrent and SQLite. The app now reads the engine through one native pump instead of several polling loops, and a browser download is released only after the engine confirms it would receive the same file. Every new download is confirmed in a standalone add window, an optional floating window shows progress over other apps, and site rules, multi-select, moving unfinished downloads and post-download actions are new. Linux rendering, start at login and file safety are fixed across the board.

### 🚀 Performance

Aria2 Next 3.0.0 against the 2.8.6 engine of Rayburst 4.0.1, measured on the same machine and network; every downloaded file was verified.

| Download | Size | 4.1.0 vs 4.0.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| openSUSE image from a Metalink with several mirrors | 261 MiB | about 20× faster |
| eMule installer over ED2K | 3.2 MiB | about 6× faster |
| Sintel torrent with a web seed | 123 MiB | about 2× faster; first data about 10× sooner |
| Linux kernel tarball from kernel.org | 149 MiB | about 1.8× faster |
| HLS and DASH streams | 4 cases | all complete; 4.0.1 failed 3 |
| Server that throttles with 503 or 429 | — | completes at the server's limit; 4.0.1 failed the task |
| One response with a wrong `Content-Range` | — | about 14× faster; 4.0.1 dropped to one connection |
| Connections that open but never send data | — | completes; 4.0.1 stalled |

- Fast single servers download at the same speed with 2–4× less CPU time and less memory.
- Downloads from one server share its connections by remaining bytes when the server limits them, so a large video no longer waits behind its audio and subtitles.
- The app reads the global status and the task lists in one call per tick, and the window no longer polls. Busy engines no longer trigger restart storms (#690).
- Large torrents stay responsive: the file selector is virtualized, and the window receives at most 64 files per task, except the task whose details are open (#447).

### 🔗 Rayburst Connect

| | Rayburst 4.0.x | Rayburst 4.1.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rayburst Connect 2.0.x | ✅ | Update the extension |
| Rayburst Connect 2.1.2 or later | ✅ | ✅ |

- **Verified handoffs:** the extension holds a browser download until Rayburst answers. Rayburst asks the engine to request the URL with the browser's headers and cookies, and takes over only when the server answers with the expected file. Web pages, rejected or unreachable URLs and size mismatches stay in the browser, and a lost answer never leaves a download in neither place.
- With the confirm behavior and Connect 2.1.4 or later, the browser releases a download as soon as the add window shows it (#720).
- The popup lists unfinished and recent tasks with pause, resume and show in folder.
- Browser `.torrent` links either open the torrent's content or are saved as plain files; they are always saved while BitTorrent is off ([connect#50](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst-connect/issues/50)).
- Starting Rayburst from Firefox works when the browser forbids leaving its job object ([connect#62](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst-connect/issues/62)).
- Media from a CDN without captured headers is requested with the page origin as Referer, so split audio and video tracks no longer answer 403.

### ✨ New Features

- **Standalone add window** — every new download, from the menu, tray, links, drops or the extension, is confirmed in one movable window that opens at once. It reads each link's size and file name the way the download will request them, shows the total against the folder's free space, and accepts dropped `.torrent` files (#693, #445, #379, #400, #718)
- **Floating window** — an optional orb that stays on top, fills with the overall progress and shows the speed. Click it for a panel to pause or resume each download, or drop links and torrents on it. Show it always, only while downloading or never; on Windows it steps aside for fullscreen apps (#718, #726)
- **Site rules** — choose the proxy and cap connections per host, for the add window and browser downloads (#489, [connect#52](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst-connect/issues/52))
- **Multi-select** — Ctrl/Shift click, Ctrl+A and Esc, with batch resume, pause and delete (#473)
- **Move unfinished downloads** — Task details → "Save to" → "Move to…" pauses the download, moves its files across disks too, and resumes it (#696)
- **Per-task speed limits** in the add window and task details, including live upload limits for BitTorrent
- **Duplicate detection** against live tasks and history, even after the earlier file was moved or deleted, with skip, add anyway or cancel (#491, #545)
- **Replace a task's URL**, or retry a failed task with a new one (#548)
- **Post-download program** with `{file}`, `{dir}` and `{name}` arguments, and **shut down when complete** from the speed popover (#651, #733)
- **Expected checksum** for single downloads, **DNS over HTTPS** with presets, and a switch to **skip certificate checks** for trusted self-signed servers (#337, #704)
- **Download torrents in order**, so files finish one after another like the episodes of a series (#703)
- **Torrent links open their file list** when copied or pasted (#737)
- **Mark unfinished files** with `.ray` until they complete, and **remove records when complete** while keeping the files (#721, #722)
- **Notifications** — clicking one on Windows shows or opens the file, and Settings says when the system turns Rayburst's notifications off, with a test notification (#609, #742)
- **Redirect target** — task details show where a redirected link leads, and the download is filed under the category of the file it delivers (#730)
- **Interface size** with Ctrl/Cmd +, − and 0, optional IEC units (KiB, MiB) and a Linux system title bar option (#367, #496, #533)
- **Tray icon** can be hidden, and shows a dot while downloads run and the speeds in its tooltip (#352, #508, #283)
- **GPU acceleration** on Linux — Settings → Advanced picks whether the graphics card or the CPU draws the window (#731)

### 🛠 Improvements

- Bundles [Aria2 Next 3.0.8](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/releases/tag/v3.0.8). It keeps an existing file intact when a server ignores ranges, writes BitTorrent names as UTF-8 under any Linux locale and names an unavailable Windows drive or network share. XML-RPC, Thunder links and the PeerBanHelper blocklist methods remain available
- Settings are reorganized so related options sit together, with shorter hints in all languages. Save and Discard appear only when something changed (#691, #723)
- The BitTorrent file selector shows a folder tree with file-type icons, type shortcuts and invert selection (#598, #472)
- Taken file names are numbered `name (1).ext`, as browsers and file managers do; a typed name is used exactly as written (#709)
- Split archive parts such as `.7z.001`, `.z01` and `.r00` are filed with the archive's category (#736)
- Clipboard detection offers file links only by default, and only links copied after Rayburst started (#683, #738)
- Lightweight mode frees every window in the tray, leaving only Rayburst and the engine; the floating window can optionally stay (#735)
- The add window, the floating window and its panel follow the system text size and interface zoom on Windows and Linux (#731)
- Esc hides the window like its close button without quitting (#569)
- Update checks finish within 15 seconds and check both channels together (#657)
- Task progress is rounded down to one decimal, so a task never reads 100% before it finishes
- History written by a newer version is kept; the notice offers an update or, after confirmation, a reset (#729)
- The engine saves unfinished tasks every 60 seconds and checkpoints progress every 10 seconds. Crash recovery stops after three crashes in five minutes
- [docs/LINUX.md](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/blob/v4.1.0/docs/LINUX.md) lists fixes for Linux display problems

### ⚠️ Changed Behavior

- **Resume downloads** is removed. A new download of an existing file name is renamed instead of continuing into that file; Retry still resumes the task's own file (#595)
- **New installs use 16 connections per file**; saved preferences keep their value
- Downloaded `.torrent` files are saved instead of started; open them to start the torrent. A new switch turns BitTorrent off entirely (#558)
- The engine maps BitTorrent and ED2K ports itself and moves to another port when one is taken; a taken RPC port falls back to a free local port. The port-conflict recovery settings are removed
- The maximum HTTP range size setting is removed; the engine sizes ranges by connection speed
- On Linux, GPU acceleration replaces the software rendering switch and is off by default. Remove WebKitGTK environment variables you added for earlier versions
- External RPC clients see the Aria2 Next 3 changes: RPC over TLS is gone, retired engine options are ignored with a warning, and Metalink 3 is no longer read. See the [engine release notes](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/releases/tag/v3.0.0)
- Settings for removed features are dropped on first start; everything else carries over, and unfinished downloads resume with their progress

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed a download continuing into another download's file of the same name, including when the server ignores ranges (#595)
- Fixed Linux windows flickering or showing only the area around the pointer with WebKitGTK 2.54: every frame is now repainted in full. WebKitGTK also keeps compositing, so translucent shadows no longer pile up (#650, #705, #731)
- Fixed the AppImage staying invisible with `EGL_BAD_PARAMETER` on newer Mesa (#714)
- Fixed KDE showing a generic icon for Rayburst, and Rayburst missing from application menus in deb and rpm installs (#745, #731)
- Fixed the main window popping up after a KDE panel restart (#707)
- Fixed start at login on Windows for install paths with spaces, such as `D:\Program Files`; the next launch repairs the entry (#716)
- Fixed "Open file" for downloads on network shares such as `\\server\share` (#715)
- Fixed notifications on Windows installs upgraded from an older product, start notifications for tasks added by any RPC client, and tasks announced as "Unknown" (#685, #534)
- Fixed a silent autostart showing a maximized window (#576)
- Fixed queued magnets showing as fetching metadata (#611)
- Fixed shortened long multibyte file names losing their extension (#509)
- Fixed seeding-only or unsized downloads animating the taskbar indefinitely
- Bounded Extension API requests in flight and their write rate (#603)

body:
## What's Changed

This beta bundles Aria2 Next 3.0.6, which shares a server's connections fairly across downloads and keeps parallel connections for servers that omit Content-Range. Lightweight mode now frees every webview in the tray, the floating orb tells seeding from downloading, and several download and add-window refinements land.

### ✨ New Features

- **Torrent links open their file list** — copying or pasting a `.torrent` link fetches it and shows its files for selection at once (#737)

- **Lightweight mode frees every webview** — the main window, the prepared add window, the floating orb and its panel all close in the tray, leaving only Rayburst and the engine; they return with the main window (#735)
- **Floating orb** — it fills from the bottom with the overall progress, shows the upload speed while only seeding, and marks connecting, queued and paused states with their sign and percentage; its panel opens centered on it and lists seeding torrents with their upload speed
- **Duplicate prompt from history** — a URL downloaded before is recognized even after its file was moved, renamed or deleted (#545)

- **Advanced options** — resource type and "save for this site" sit lower, next to the options they belong to

- Fixed the main window appearing transparent and empty for a moment on launch and when reopened from the tray
- Fixed the macOS traffic lights drifting off the add window's title bar; on macOS the add window is now framed like the main window

name: v4.1.0-beta.6 — Floating Window, Instant Add Window and Thunder Links
body:
## What's Changed

A floating speed window, a new-task window that appears instantly and shows each download's size before it starts, moving unfinished downloads to another folder, and Thunder links working again. The bundled engine moves to aria2-next 3.0.4.

### ✨ New Features

- **Floating window** — an optional orb that stays on top with the overall speed ringed by progress; click it for a panel to pause or resume each download, drag it anywhere (Settings → General → Tray & Dock → "Floating window") (#718)

- **Move unfinished downloads** — Task details → "Save to" → "Move to…": a running download pauses, its files move (across disks too) and it resumes (#696)
- **Mark unfinished files** — Settings → Downloads: unfinished downloads end in `.ray` until they complete (#721)
- **Remove records when complete** — "Keep completed records" can now remove a record as soon as the download finishes; files stay (#722)

### 🛠 Improvements

- Bundled engine updated to [aria2-next 3.0.4](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/releases/tag/v3.0.4)
- The new-task window is prepared at startup and only hidden when closed, so it appears without delay, with a smoother entrance
- Taken file names are numbered `name (1).ext`, as browsers and file managers do (#709)
- A typed file name is used exactly as written, extension included; "Look up filename" became "Refresh"
- The connections field shows the cap a site rule applies and names the rule (#719)
- Save and Discard in Settings appear only when something changed and slide in; "Save & Apply" is now "Apply" (#723)
- DNS-over-HTTPS presets reach their resolvers by IP address, so finding the resolver needs no plain DNS lookup
- With the browser extension 2.1.4, the browser releases a download as soon as the Rayburst dialog shows it (#720)
- Transparent windows are back on Linux; the panels that blurred their background use a plain translucent one (#705, #650)
- After a KDE panel restart, the main window no longer pops up; it shows only if the tray stays gone for 10 s (#707)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed Thunder (`thunder://`) links failing with "Unsupported URI"
- Fixed every failed submission in the new-task window being reported as "The engine is starting"
- Fixed start at login on Windows still failing silently: the entry no longer carries the `\\?\` prefix Explorer cannot start; the next launch repairs it (#716)

### 📦 Downloads

name: v4.1.0-beta.1 — Rebuilt Engine, Major Speedups and Verified Browser Handoffs
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Please pair this beta with Rayburst Connect 2.1.0.** Browser handoff was rebuilt for this release. Rather than keep the old handoff path alongside the new one, we chose to keep both apps lean, so Rayburst 4.1.0 and Rayburst Connect 2.1.0 work with each other but not with the earlier versions. Until both are updated, the extension shows "Desktop version not supported" and the browser simply keeps its downloads. The browser stores still list 2.0.6, so install 2.1.0 from its [GitHub Release](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst-connect/releases/tag/v2.1.0) for now.

## What's Changed

Rayburst 4.1.0 is the largest update since 4.0: it moves to the rebuilt Aria2 Next 3.0.0 engine, rebuilds how the app supervises the engine and how browser downloads are handed over, and brings the biggest download speedups the project has had. The engine replaces the event loop inherited from aria2 with a new core (Boost.Asio, libcurl, libtorrent, SQLite) at about a quarter of the previous code. The app now reads the engine through one native pump instead of several polling loops, and a browser download is released only after the engine confirms it would receive the same file. This beta also adds a standalone add window, per-site rules, multi-select, post-download actions and more than forty fixes.

### 🚀 Performance

Aria2 Next 3.0.0 against the 2.8.6 engine of Rayburst 4.0.1, measured on the same machine and network; every downloaded file was verified.

| Download | Size | 4.1.0 vs 4.0.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| openSUSE image from a Metalink with several mirrors | 261 MiB | about 20× faster |
| eMule installer over ED2K | 3.2 MiB | about 6× faster |
| Sintel torrent with a web seed | 123 MiB | about 2× faster; first data about 10× sooner |
| Linux kernel tarball from kernel.org | 149 MiB | about 1.8× faster |
| HLS and DASH streams | 4 cases | all complete; 4.0.1 failed 3 |
| Server that throttles with 503 or 429 | — | completes at the server's limit; 4.0.1 failed the task |
| One response with a wrong `Content-Range` | — | about 14× faster; 4.0.1 dropped to one connection |
| Connections that open but never send data | — | completes; 4.0.1 stalled |

- Fast single servers download at the same speed with 2–4× less CPU time and less memory.
- HTTP downloads open every configured connection at once. Servers that throttle (429/503), misreport ranges or stall a connection no longer fail the task or drop it to a single connection.
- The app reads the global status and the task lists in one call per tick, and the window no longer polls. Busy engines no longer trigger restart storms (#690).
- Large torrents stay responsive: the file selector is virtualized, and the window receives at most 64 files per task, except the task whose details are open (#447).

### 🔗 Rayburst Connect

| | Rayburst 4.0.x | Rayburst 4.1.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rayburst Connect 2.0.x | ✅ | Update the extension |
| Rayburst Connect 2.1.0 | Update Rayburst | ✅ |

- **Verified handoffs:** the extension holds a browser download until Rayburst answers. Rayburst asks the engine to request the URL with the browser's headers and cookies, and takes over only when the server answers with the expected file. Web pages, rejected or unreachable URLs and size mismatches stay in the browser, and a lost answer never leaves a download in neither place.
- The popup lists unfinished and recent tasks with pause, resume and show in folder.
- Browser `.torrent` links either open the torrent's content or are saved as plain files; they are always saved while BitTorrent is off ([connect#50](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst-connect/issues/50)).
- Site rules choose the proxy per host and can cap connections per server ([connect#52](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst-connect/issues/52), #489).
- Starting Rayburst from Firefox works when the browser forbids leaving its job object ([connect#62](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst-connect/issues/62)).
- Media from a CDN without captured headers is requested with the page origin as Referer, as browsers do, so split audio and video tracks no longer answer 403.

### ⚠️ Changed Behavior

- The UPnP and port-conflict recovery settings are removed. The engine maps BitTorrent and ED2K ports itself and moves to another port when one is taken; a taken RPC port falls back to a free local port.
- Downloaded `.torrent` files are saved instead of started; open them to start the torrent. A new BitTorrent switch turns BitTorrent off entirely (#558).
- External RPC clients see the Aria2 Next 3.0.0 changes: XML-RPC and RPC over TLS are gone, and retired engine options are ignored with a warning. See the [engine release notes](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/releases/tag/v3.0.0).
- Settings for removed features are dropped on first start; everything else carries over.

### ✨ New Features

- **Standalone add window** for browser downloads that arrive while the main window is hidden or closed, showing the batch size and the free space of the target drive (#693, #445, #379, #400).
- **Site rules** with per-host connection caps and proxy choice, applied to the add dialog and browser downloads (#489).
- **Multi-select** with Ctrl/Shift click, Ctrl+A and Esc, with batch resume, pause and delete (#473).
- **Per-task speed limits** in the add dialog and task details, including live upload limits for BitTorrent.
- **Duplicate detection** against live tasks and history, with skip, add anyway or cancel (#491).
- **Replace a task's URL**, or retry a failed task with a new one (#548).
- **Post-download program** with `{file}`, `{dir}` and `{name}` arguments (#651).
- **Expected checksum** for single downloads, and **DNS over HTTPS** with presets (#337).
- **Clickable notifications** on Windows that reveal the finished file (#609).
- **Interface size** setting with Ctrl/Cmd +, − and 0 (#367), optional IEC units (KiB, MiB) (#496) and a Linux system title bar option (#533).
- **Tray icon** can be hidden, and shows a dot while downloads run and the speeds in its tooltip (#352, #508, #283).

### 🛠 Improvements

- The BitTorrent file selector is redesigned with a folder tree, file-type icons, type shortcuts and invert selection (#598, #472).
- Esc hides the window like its close button without quitting (#569).
- Clipboard detection offers file links only by default (#683).
- The engine saves unfinished tasks every 60 seconds and checkpoints progress every 10 seconds, so a crash or power loss loses little.
- The sidecar is stopped through its own process handle, and a restart never overlaps a running engine. Crash recovery stops after three crashes in five minutes.
- Update checks finish within 15 seconds and check both channels together (#657).
- [docs/LINUX.md](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/blob/main/docs/LINUX.md) lists workarounds for blank windows, stutter and WebKit crashes on Linux.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Notifications show on Windows installs upgraded from an older product (#685), tasks added by any RPC client announce their start (#534), and a started task is announced by its real name instead of "Unknown".
- A silent autostart no longer shows a maximized window (#576).
- Queued magnets show as queued instead of fetching metadata (#611).
- Shortening a long multibyte filename keeps its extension (#509).
- Seeding-only or unsized downloads no longer animate the taskbar indefinitely.
- Extension API requests in flight and their write rate are bounded (#603).

name: v4.0.0 — Introducing Rayburst: Native Media Downloads and Browser Integration
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Motrix Next is now Rayburst.** Settings, tasks and history are not imported into the new application.
>
> Before switching, finish active downloads, back up unfinished work, and quit and uninstall Motrix Next. Install Rayburst and configure it again. Keep your downloaded files. Updating through the old app may leave both applications installed or retain old shortcuts.
>
> **Coming from an early 4.0 beta?** Review custom file categories in Settings → Downloads. Each rule now needs a relative or absolute directory mode. Classification sets the destination before downloading; it no longer moves completed files.

## What's Changed

Rayburst 4.0 introduces native HLS/DASH downloads, live recording and a unified sidebar. It brings the six beta releases to the stable channel, with Aria2 Next 2.8.2 and fixes for download recovery, browser handoff and desktop integration.

### ✨ New Features

- **Media downloads:** select video, audio and subtitle tracks from HLS and MPEG-DASH sources. Save compatible output as MP4, MKV or subtitle-only WebVTT without a separate downloader.
- **Live recording:** set a duration or choose **Finish recording and save**. Pause and retry media tasks using their existing recovery data.
- **Browser media capture:** receive manifests, compatible media fragments and recordings from Rayburst Connect. Confirming a selection in the extension starts the same task without another desktop prompt.
- **Remember save location:** optionally reuse the last directory you selected. Browser submissions follow this preference without changing it.
- **HTTP range limit:** set a maximum size for individual HTTP range requests. Leave it at `0` for automatic sizing.

### 🛠 Improvements

- Combine task filters, About and Settings in one sidebar, with a compact layout for narrow windows and coordinated page, toolbar and footer transitions.
- Apply theme colors throughout the light and dark interfaces. Refine the default purple palette and add default and dark macOS icon appearances.
- Handle submissions, confirmation receipts, history and notifications in Rust while the main window is closed. Retrying a browser handoff after a lost reply reuses its submission identity.
- Start the desktop installation paired with the browser's Native Messaging host without relying on URL-handler defaults.
- Show native association status and repair actions for `.torrent`, `magnet`, `ed2k`, `thunder` and `rayburst`.
- Open completed or seeding content by double-clicking its task. List recent save directories in most-recent-first order.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Prevent completed HTTP downloads from reappearing after a crash.
- Keep duplicate-torrent errors from failing the original task, and preserve torrent directories and per-task limits when global settings change.
- Restart eligible partial HTTP downloads when the remote resource changes, without mixing data from different versions of the file.
- Protect files used by other tasks during deletion. Keep the history entry if file removal fails.
- Pause seeding when downloaded files become missing or inaccessible, including while the window is closed. Recheck affected torrents when they resume.
- Fix window recreation in lightweight mode and allow browser submissions to receive acknowledgements without waiting for the window.
- Normalize proxy bypass lists and supported IPv4 wildcard rules. Report unsupported imported rules for correction.
- Report engine startup and failure separately from desktop connection failures, so Rayburst Connect can offer recovery instead of repeatedly launching the app.

name: v4.0.0-beta.6 — Download Recovery and Theme Consistency
body:
## What's Changed

This beta improves task recovery, file ownership and browser handoff diagnostics, and bundles Aria2 Next 2.8.2 for all six desktop targets. It also adds optional save-location memory and completes the light and dark theme integration.

### ✨ New Features

- **Remember save location:** optionally reuse the last directory explicitly chosen for a successful submission. Browser submissions use the same preference without changing it. The setting is off by default; unavailable directories are reported instead of silently replaced.
- **HTTP range limit:** configure the maximum size of each HTTP range request in Download settings. `0` keeps automatic sizing; a value such as `5M` accommodates servers with request-size limits. Media segments, SFTP and torrent piece sizes are unaffected.
- **Open downloaded content:** double-click completed or seeding task cards in either layout to open their content. Buttons and text selection retain their existing behavior.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Delete task files by their recorded paths and GID. Protect files referenced by other tasks, retain history when file deletion fails, and stop removing or hiding separate tasks solely because they share a torrent hash.
- Detect missing or inaccessible completed files through native filesystem monitoring, including while the main window is closed. Pause affected seeding tasks and request a BitTorrent recheck when they resume.
- Move download-start notifications into the native task lifecycle, covering silent browser submissions and respecting the notification switches. Metadata fetching no longer serves as the start-notification trigger.
- Restore recreated windows on the main event thread after plugin initialization, avoiding the lock-order conflict between lightweight mode and saved window state.
- Convert supported Windows IPv4 proxy-bypass patterns to CIDR and report unsupported imported rules. Disabled proxies no longer validate unused bypass entries; invalid active configurations direct users to Network settings.

name: v4.0.0-beta.1 — Introducing Rayburst and Native Media Downloads
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **The first release under the Rayburst name.** Rayburst 4.0.0-beta.1 introduces the new desktop identity and native streaming-media downloads, paired with Rayburst Connect 2.0.0. This is a **beta release**.

> [!CAUTION]
> **A fresh installation is recommended when moving from Motrix Next.** The application identifier, installation names and data directories have changed. In-app updating may fail to replace the old application or leave both applications installed. Previous settings, task state and history are not imported automatically.

## Before installing

1. Finish active downloads and recordings in the previous application. Keep a backup of its application data and any unfinished downloads before uninstalling.
2. Quit the previous application, including its tray process. Uninstall it, then install the Rayburst package for your operating system and architecture. Keep downloaded files and your backup.
3. Configure Rayburst again. Install Rayburst Connect 2.0.0 and reconnect it using Rayburst's Extension API address and secret. Disable the previous extension to avoid competing download interception.

This beta uses the prerelease update channel; the stable channel remains separate. Automatic updates across the brand migration are not a substitute for the installation steps above. Linux packages require glibc 2.35 or newer and a compatible system C++ runtime, matching Ubuntu 22.04.

## What's changed

### Native streaming-media downloads

- Bundle **Aria2 Next 2.8.0** on all six desktop targets. HLS and MPEG-DASH manifests are inspected and downloaded inside the engine, using GPAC, libcurl, OpenSSL and FFmpeg.
- Select video, audio and subtitle tracks before downloading. Save compatible output as MP4, Matroska or subtitle-only WebVTT, with finite time ranges aligned to media segments.
- Record live streams with a duration limit or use **Finish recording and save**. Live tasks show recorded duration; finalization does not invent a completion percentage.
- Pause and retry media tasks through the engine's recovery state. Track selection stays attached to the same task, and restored tasks do not repeatedly open selection dialogs.
- Receive browser-captured manifests, compatible fragment collections and recordings from Rayburst Connect. Inspection and confirmation share one task, without a second desktop selection prompt.

### Rayburst identity and interface

- Introduce the Rayburst name, logo, application identity, package names, website and localized copy.
- Use a softer purple default through the existing Material Design color system. Empty download lists can display the brand mark; the setting can be turned off.
- Refresh task snapshots every 500 ms and simplify task refresh coordination. Media tasks expose recording, selection and retry actions alongside ordinary download controls.

### Download ownership and recovery

- Move ordinary task submission, confirmation receipts and history ownership into Rust. Browser handoff and completion persistence remain available when the main window is closed.
- Preserve submission identities when replies are lost, so reconciliation does not create a second download. Keep browser credentials scoped to their observed request origins.
- Let the engine resolve filenames and output collisions. Preserve browser filename hints and media titles across restart.
- Include the engine fix for BitTorrent progress freezing after hash failures or file-selection changes.

### Media limits

DRM, subtitle translation and transcoding are not supported. Container compatibility depends on the selected codecs. Fragment collections must contain compatible media in playback order; this is not an arbitrary video-joining tool. Live recovery cannot restore segments the server has already removed.

See the [media guide](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/blob/v4.0.0-beta.1/docs/MEDIA.md) and [engine release notes](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/releases/tag/v2.8.0).

name: v3.9.9 — More Reliable Downloads, Smoother Everyday Use
body:
## What's Changed

Motrix Next 3.9.9 brings the improvements from the 3.9.9 beta cycle to the stable channel, with Aria2 Next 2.7.5, more resilient HTTP transfers, consistent task history, smoother task cards, and more reliable desktop integration.

### 🛠 Improvements

- **HTTP transfer recovery** — Improved parallel-download concurrency recovery, redirect destination reuse, IPv4/IPv6 worker scheduling, and stalled-tail recovery while respecting connection limits and retry backoff
- **Consistent task lists** — Unified live-task and history sorting, snapshots, and sidebar counts; removed the 1,000-entry limit from active and waiting task snapshots
- **Smoother task cards** — Added filename and status transitions, refined progress and action animations, and preserved card identity and manual ordering when retrying tasks
- **Compact layout** — Stabilized progress-bar width with a fixed percentage gap and right-aligned transfer details, keeping the two-line layout and revealing truncated details through tooltips
- **Actionable diagnostics** — Added browser-launcher registration details, native OS errors, and Linux protocol-handler information to diagnostic exports

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed HTTP scheduling defects that unnecessarily reduced parallelism after early 403 responses or mishandled 429/503 overload responses
- Fixed false resource-change failures involving unquoted ETags and inconsistent CDN timestamps, including the reported Baidu Netdisk case; improved conditional range handling at redirecting endpoints
- Fixed a Windows engine event-loop crash and preserved pending wakeups when libcurl reschedules timers
- Fixed tasks briefly disappearing between engine completion and history persistence, suppressed stale duplicate BT/ED2K results, and preserved partial progress and error details in newly recorded history
- Fixed one browser's Native Messaging registration failure blocking registration for other browsers
- Prevented browser-inherited `EGL_PLATFORM` settings from interfering with Linux desktop activation
- Reworked Linux link associations around native GIO/XDG handling, including desktop-specific defaults and persistent AppImage paths; failed status queries now offer retry instead of appearing disabled
- Fixed saved window decorations overriding platform settings and hiding macOS traffic-light controls ([#587](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/motrix-next/issues/587))
- Fixed compact progress bars changing length as transfer metadata updates ([#589](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/motrix-next/issues/589))
